before: == compares reference identity for objects. equals can define logical equality. A record’s generated equals compares corresponding components, so two separate Key(7) instances are equal.
HashSet uses hashing and equality to detect duplicates. Do not change fields that participate in equality while an object is a hash-based key; this record’s primitive component is stable.

Optional local transfer task: Verify equal records have equal hash codes without predicting a universal numeric hash formula. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: For objects, == asks whether references point to the same object. equals can ask whether their data counts as equal. Key's generated record method compares its id values, so two separate Keys with the same id are equal.

A hash code is an integer used to help find objects in collections. Equal objects must have the same hash code. Different objects may also share one, so it is not a unique ID. Records generate matching equals and hashCode behavior.

HashSet uses both hash codes and equals to spot repeated members. Data used by those methods should stay unchanged while an object is stored as a key. Key's final int component keeps that data stable here.
The program prints false, true, and 1 on separate lines. a and b are separate objects with equal ids, so the set keeps one equal member.
The quiz changes b's id. Check equality from the component values, then decide whether the set sees a repeated member.

before.question: Give b the id 8. What changes in equals and the set size?
choices: equals is false and size is 2
equals is false but all record hashes must be unique
equals stays true and size stays 1
before.explanation: Different id components make the records unequal. Both distinct logical keys remain in the set; this does not require unique hashes for all possible records.

after.question: Give b the id 8. What happens to a.equals(b) and the set size?
choices: equals is false and the size is two.
equals is false, so every possible record must have a unique hash code.
equals stays true and the size stays one.
after.explanation: The ids now differ, so the Keys are unequal and both remain in the set. This does not require all hash codes to be unique.
